bug_semantics: CWE-601 open redirect (and cache-poisoning amplifier) in @angular/ssr: an unsanitized X-Forwarded-Prefix is passed into joinUrlParts() and then addLeadingSlash() when emitting a redirect Location. addLeadingSlash only treats a leading '/' as already-absolute, so a prefix of '\evil.com' becomes '/\evil.com'. Browsers treat the '/\' sequence as a protocol-relative '//', sending the client to the attacker host. After CVE-2026-27738, INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX /^[/\\]{2}/ rejected two leading slash-or-backslash characters (//, \\, /\, \\/) but still accepted a single leading backslash; the same prepend-slash transform therefore remained exploitable. Redirects also omitted Vary: X-Forwarded-Prefix, so a poisoned Location could be cached.
flaw_origin: The protocol-relative Location sink was first written on 2025-11-21 in 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41 (PR #31904, Closes #31902): AngularServerApp.handle() started calling createRedirectResponse(joinUrlParts(request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-Prefix') ?? '', buildPathWithParams(...))). The parent still emitted Location from the path only. Pre-existing joinUrlParts/addLeadingSlash (url.ts) stripped/tested only '/', so '\evil.com'+'/home' already produced '/\evil.com/home' at this first wiring. CVE-2026-27738's f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323 later added INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX /^[/\\]{2}/ and tests for '//evil','\\evil','/\\evil','\\/evil' but not '\evil'; that incomplete control did not create the '/\' transform and is not the BIC. Backports of the sink (cceb8629 on 20.3.x, 03e23121 on 21.0.x) are cherry-picks, not first writes.

evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-33397 state=PUBLISHED (cvelistV5 2026-03-30, not rejected); GHSA-vfx2-hv2g-xj5f withdrawn_at=null; NVD/OSV alias the same GHSA. Real incomplete-fix open redirect of CVE-2026-27738, not a false positive.

Attack: AngularServerApp.handle() uses joinUrlParts(X-Forwarded-Prefix, redirect path) as Location. At BIC, packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts:179-186 wires the header; url.ts addLeadingSlash (lines 59-61) returns `/${url}` unless url[0]==='/'; joinUrlParts (lines 97-117) strips only leading '/'. Prefix '\evil.com' + '/home' => '/\evil.com/home'. Browsers interpret '/\' as '//'.

git log -L '/redirectTo !== undefined/,+15:packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts' first adds the prefix sink in 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41 (2025-11-21, PR https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/31904). Immediate parent 59319b8d6f02f857ab375f330812ff430e90f059 still has createRedirectResponse(buildPathWithParams(redirectTo, url.pathname), status) with no X-Forwarded-Prefix. git grep X-Forwarded-Prefix 4dac5f25^ -- packages/angular/ssr is empty.

Incomplete CVE-2026-27738 control f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323 (2026-02-23, PR #32521) first wrote INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX = /^[/\\]{2}|(?:^|[/\\])\.\.?(?:[/\\]|$)/ and tests ['//evil','\\evil','/\\evil','\\/evil'] — two-char slash/backslash only. joinUrlParts after that strip still leaves '\evil.com' and addLeadingSlash still prepends '/'. Not a first-write of the '/\' mechanism; original workaround even used replace(/^[/\\]+/, '/') which would have caught a single backslash, unlike the shipped regex.

Direct fix 4d564f66f694011724d4933bf025f1c4fed55bca (PR https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/32771) changes INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX to /^(?:\\|\/[/\\])|(?:^|[/\\])\.\.?(?:[/\\]|$)/ and adds test input '\evil'. Ancestor of v22.0.0-next.2, not of v22.0.0-next.1. Branch copies: f3e0e82c2cecc3d9ebb5b8acc6e64d2d88c4efbd (cherry-pick, v21.2.3), 1dc6992a5ae6c5a1f16f22f6c94690d5cf218c38 (v20.3.21). Sibling 998b8298e3106c95d77ced8090ab815365c462c7 adds Vary: X-Forwarded-Prefix on redirect responses.

reasoning: GHSA-vfx2-hv2g-xj5f / CVE-2026-33397 is a published open-redirect via X-Forwarded-Prefix starting with a single backslash. The distinctive Location transform is joinUrlParts(untrusted prefix) then addLeadingSlash, which prepends '/' when the first character is '\'. git log -L / -S and parent-tree grep show that composition first appearing in 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41; at 59319b8d6f02f857ab375f330812ff430e90f059 the redirect Location is path-only and packages/angular/ssr contains no X-Forwarded-Prefix. That BIC is a single-parent, single-commit PR (#31904), not a squash/move/revert. f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323 is the later incomplete CVE-2026-27738 patch: it added /^[/\\]{2}/ validation that still lets '\evil' through and did not change the prepend-'/' behavior for that payload, so it is not the first write of this mechanism. 4d564f66f694011724d4933bf025f1c4fed55bca is the smallest main-line commit that rejects a leading backslash and is the patched boundary for 22.0.0-next.2, with cherry-picks on 21.2.3 and 20.3.21.
